title: Long Call Measurement
eyebrow: Findings · can work always be split into short visible steps? Measured 2026-10-28

short.lead: I had said that almost all of my work can be split into short visible steps, but that was my judgement, not a measurement. I then measured it against the records in this container, and it is not proven. Full detail: docs/generated/2026-10-28-long-call-measurement.md.
short.hint: Tap a row for the source and what it shows.
items: This session: 0 of 38 calls over 30 seconds

Exact start and end times from this session's transcript, read by docs/generated/2026-10-28-call_durations.py. The longest were the two editor helpers, at 22.2 and 19.3 seconds. This session was planning work, so it is one light sample.
Full test run: 130 to 197 seconds, and it splits

docs/4-systems/verify-suites.md:125 and :651. If you run one part at a time with --parts, the longest part takes about 32 seconds (verify-suites.md:227). The run's output file stops growing until a part ends, so each status check must also count the running processes to show it is still working.
docs/6-decisions/Decisions.md, entry 2026-10-01. Work is split into issues of three steps or fewer, but while the helper runs, its own steps never show in this thread.
It records only when each turn started, not when each command started or ended, so it holds no per-call timings.

Those game projects are not in this container, so I have nothing to measure. A single compile cannot be cut up into shorter steps. It can only run in the background while I check on it in short status checks.
Pick how to measure a building session in the Choices section below.

choices: How do I measure a real building session?

wrapup.summary: Short steps are proven for the test suite. Helpers are split into issues, but their steps stay unseen inside each issue. Single builds cannot be split and can only be watched.
wrapup.changing: Nothing in the plugin has changed yet. The findings and the script are committed as 8c61244.
